learningObjective: Describe IREE's design as an MLIR-based end-to-end compilation and runtime stack with an explicit compiler/runtime separation and a hardware abstraction layer (HAL).

canonicalClaims.claim: IREE is an MLIR-based end-to-end compilation stack whose runtime consists of a bytecode VM plus a Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) that portably drives multiple backends (Vulkan, CUDA, ROCm, CPU, WebGPU).
conditions: The input is one of the supported dialects (StableHLO, TOSA, Torch-MLIR).
nonImplications: Does not imply IREE is the fastest option for every target.
Does not imply IREE is the only MLIR-based ML compiler.

misconceptions.claim: IREE is a Python-only JIT that only targets NVIDIA GPUs.
IREE is a thin wrapper over cuDNN.
misconceptions.whyWrong: IREE has its own codegen path via MLIR dialects.

misconceptions.claim: IREE requires a Python runtime at deployment.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The IREE runtime is a C runtime; Python is only used at build/test time.
